cf.title: Persist slot invalidations before publishing them

input.subject: Persist slot invalidations before publishing them

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the master design; three reviewers accept the approach through v11. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is fixable: 0001 changes who holds io_in_progress_lock and is proposed for backpatch to 14, but versions for 14 to 18 do not exist. A committer who knows the slot code has to agree to the locking change and the backpatch range.

brief.title: Persist replication slot invalidations to disk before publishing them
brief.problem: An inactive replication slot is marked invalid in shared memory before its state file is saved. If the save fails or the server crashes first, horizon computations may already have removed WAL or rows, and restart restores the old valid slot. In synchronize_one_slot() a failed save also blocks a direct retry, because the next sync sees the local slot as already invalid.
brief.proposed_design: A new ReplicationSlotPersistInvalidation() writes and fsyncs an invalidated copy of the acquired slot while the shared slot stays valid, then publishes the invalidation. The slot's io_in_progress_lock is held until publication, and it also serializes concurrent internal invalidators so the second one waits instead of signalling the first. The fix covers InvalidatePossiblyObsoleteSlot() (0001) and synchronize_one_slot() (0002).
user_visible_surface: C API: new ReplicationSlotPersistInvalidation() declared in replication/slot.h.
Wait event ReplicationSlotIO can now appear for a second invalidator waiting on the same slot.
New injection point in the slot invalidation path, used by the tests.
author_claims: The on-disk slot format and the ReplicationSlot shared memory layout do not change, which eases backpatching.
A failed save leaves both the shared slot and its disk image valid, and a later checkpoint or sync retries without a new retry mechanism.
0001 should be backpatched to 14 and 0002 to 17; versions 14 and 15 need adaptation.
Rui Zhao measured a checkpoint pass over 100 valid physical slots going from 7.2 us to 9.0 us with the locking change.
On a hot standby, connections can use a restored valid slot before the next restartpoint detects the invalidation again.
brief.thread_state: Rui Zhao, shveta malik and Ashutosh Sharma reviewed through v11 and say the approach and code look good, after the locking fix for concurrent invalidators was folded in. Horiguchi proposed a separate invalidation file and Zhijie Hou an in-memory durability flag; the author argued against both, and the latest messages are rebases.
unclear: No backpatch versions exist yet for 14 to 18, so the adaptations for 14 and 15 are unknown.
The window in synchronize_one_slot() between acquiring the slot and taking the lock still lets a restartpoint terminate the slot sync worker; nobody says whether to fix it.
No committer has stated a position on the design or on backpatching to 14.
A failed save deletes a temporary synchronized slot, and nobody says whether that outcome is acceptable.

objections.title: Backpatch of a new slot locking protocol to 14 without branch versions
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 14 or 15 installs a minor release that carries the adapted 0001. The checkpointer now takes each slot's io_in_progress_lock during invalidation, and an unreviewed back-branch difference in the slot code makes it wait or deadlock. The user sees checkpoints stall after a routine minor upgrade.
objections.argument: 0001 changes who holds io_in_progress_lock and for how long, and it adds a wait-and-restart loop that drops ReplicationSlotControlLock (message #10). That protocol was reviewed on master only, and versions for 14 to 18 do not exist (messages #2, #3). Message #1 says 14 and 15 need adaptation that nobody has examined. A committer would likely want to see each branch version before agreeing to Backpatch-through: 14, since a locking change in a minor release is hard to take back.
objections.author_must_show: What do the 14 and 15 versions of 0001 look like, and does the lock-ordering argument from message #10 hold unchanged on each branch?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 defers the branch versions until the master fix is agreed, which is usual practice but does not answer the request. Message #1 says 14 and 15 need adaptation, and the lock-ordering argument in message #10 was checked on master only.

refuted.title: New lock-ordering rule exists only in the thread
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds code that takes ReplicationSlotControlLock inside a slot save path, or a new invalidation caller that does not follow the caller-owns-the-I/O-lock contract. The checkpointer and an invalidator then deadlock, or a stale slot image is written after publication. This shows up as a rare hang in the field, not in a test.
refuted.argument: Deadlock freedom rests on the rule that no holder of an io_in_progress_lock takes ReplicationSlotControlLock (message #10, point c). The proposal also makes callers of ReplicationSlotPersistInvalidation() acquire and release the I/O lock themselves (messages #13, #20). Message #24 calls this machinery heavy, and message #38 notes SaveSlotToPathInternal() branches on the two save paths. The prose does not say where the rule is recorded, or how a future patch that breaks it would fail loudly.
refuted.author_must_show: Where is the io_in_progress_lock versus ReplicationSlotControlLock ordering rule written down, and what fails loudly if a future caller breaks it?

critic.reasoning: Messages #31, #38 and #39 show assertions on I/O lock ownership at each layer, so a caller that breaks the contract fails in assert builds. Postgres enforces no LWLock ordering rule at run time, and where the comment sits is a code-level question.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The patch changes when the slot state file is written and fsynced; the file format stays the same.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes replication slot invalidation in slot.c and slot synchronization in slotsync.c.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds ReplicationSlotPersistInvalidation() to replication/slot.h, also in back branches.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001 targets 14 and 0002 targets 17, and no branch versions exist for 14 to 18.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a locking protocol on io_in_progress_lock for invalidators and two injection-point TAP tests.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The checkpoint pass over 100 valid physical slots went from 7.2 us to 9.0 us.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What do the 14 and 15 versions of 0001 look like, and does the lock-ordering argument from message #10 hold unchanged on each branch?
Should the patch close the window in synchronize_one_slot() where a restartpoint can terminate the slot sync worker between acquiring the slot and taking the lock?
Is it acceptable that a failed save deletes a temporary synchronized slot?
On a hot standby, what stops a connection from using a restored valid slot before the next restartpoint detects the invalidation again?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows replication slot locking, checkpointer slot invalidation and slot synchronization. The brief says no committer has stated a position on the design or the backpatch.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a changed io_in_progress_lock protocol in the checkpointer path on every supported branch back to 14, for the life of those branches, plus the stability of two injection-point tests.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered reviews, folded in the fix for concurrent invalidators and kept rebasing through v11. Message #3 promises branch versions once the master fix is agreed.

priority.reason: The bug can restore a valid slot after its WAL or rows were removed, so it matters to users of replication slots. Review on master has converged; the entry waits on a committer and on branch versions for 14 to 18.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the lock ordering, the error-path cleanup and the stability of the injection-point tests are unchecked. The backpatch could not be judged because versions for 14 to 18 do not exist.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Upper limit arguments of pg_logical_slot_xxx_changes functions accept invalid values
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_logical_slot_get_changes_guts() set upto_nchanges to 0 instead of InvalidXLogRecPtr when the argument is NULL. It also rejects negative upto_nchanges values and invalid upto_lsn values with an error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier noted that a negative upto_nchanges can reasonably mean unlimited, and the author then offered to fix only the InvalidXLogRecPtr assignment. Robert Haas argued that the current code is no less robust than the proposed form and should stay as it is. Michael Paquier closed the entry because the existing behavior has been in place for several releases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I am not prepared to spend much time arguing about it, but I think we
should just leave this the way it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function pg_advance_replication_slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL function that moves a physical replication slot forward to a given WAL position without consuming the WAL, for example to keep slots in sync across servers. Later versions named it pg_advance_replication_slot, allowed forward moves only, and raised an error on logical slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked that moving the slot backwards raise an error with the current slot position instead of a warning, and that the logical-slot error use ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Andres Freund added that neither message followed the message style guidelines. The patch got no update in the following two months, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
True as well, and the patch did not get an update in two months to
reflect that. So I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client-side tool, pg_replslotdata, reads the binary replication slot files under pg_replslot/ and prints slot information such as restart LSN, xid, slot type and two-phase state. It works while the server is down, in the same way as pg_controldata and pg_waldump.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers judged that the use cases did not justify the cost of maintaining a separate tool in core, including its documentation and translations, and that most needs can be met with an online server. Since the tool is entirely client side, reviewers suggested keeping it in an external repository. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Weighed against the cost of maintaining (including documentation) a separate
tool this doesn't seem sufficient reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix slotsync worker busy loop causing repeated log messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a slotsync worker loop that logs four logical decoding messages every 200 ms when confirmed_flush_lsn matches the primary but restart_lsn does not. update_local_synced_slot() would report "no update" in that case so the worker uses the normal sleep interval, and a second patch lowered the logical decoding messages from LOG to DEBUG1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Amit Kapila questioned how 0001 detected an update and opposed the log-level change in 0002. The thread then settled on a simpler patch by Zhijie Hou that compares the slot's old and new LSN/xmin, and Hou posted it for HEAD and back branches.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejected the idea of persisting a slot invalidation before publishing it. P3 and P8 were test reverts, which are an implementation-level concern outside this review, and P2 rejected a different change to physical slot behaviour. Message #1 cites the commits that introduced the current ordering, not earlier attempts to change it.

The proposal changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, dumped object, psql behaviour or wire message, and it keeps the on-disk slot format and the ReplicationSlot layout, so back branches see no contract change. The only client-visible effects are a ReplicationSlotIO wait in a rare race and a slot that stays valid after a failed save, which fixes the current state. The 14 and 15 backpatch versions do not exist yet, so their compatibility could not be checked.

No objection from the replication and on-disk angle. The proposal keeps the slot state file format and the ReplicationSlot shared memory layout, adds no WAL record, catalog or protocol change, and leaves pg_upgrade untouched. It moves only the ordering, so an invalid image reaches disk before horizons stop counting the slot. The new disk-ahead-of-memory window fails safe: a crash there restores an invalid slot, and the invalidation was already decided. Thread messages #10 and #23 found and settled the concurrent-invalidator termination and the temporary synchronized slot case. The slot sync worker window in message #10 (d) also exists on master. The 14 and 15 backport versions do not exist yet, so the backport cannot be checked.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It reorders a slot state write before publication inside slot.c and slotsync.c, adds no SQL interface, role, GUC or view column, and changes nothing a non-superuser can do or see. The new io_in_progress_lock wait happens only between internal invalidators, so an unprivileged session cannot hold it to block them.
The fix is a bugfix in a narrow path. The hot-path cost is small and shown (message #10), and it adds no new dependency. Remaining concerns are backpatch scope and keeping the locking rule explicit.

This is a crash-durability bug fix inside slot.c and slotsync.c, and no existing feature, setting or extension can change the order in which core saves and publishes a slot invalidation. The patch also reuses existing mechanisms, the slot state file and io_in_progress_lock, so it adds no second mechanism for the same job.

This is a durability bugfix, so demand does not need to come from field reports. The thread shows a concrete failure: a failed save or crash leaves a valid slot on disk after its WAL or rows were removed, and on master a failed save leaves the slot stuck active (message #10). Several independent reviewers agree the problem is real. The cost falls on the invalidation path and a small checkpoint pass overhead, so a demand-based objection would not hold.
